title: FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit Record and the PracticePay Payoff Good-Through Days
content:
**Rule.** In PracticePay Patient Financing, the FlexLine extra good-through days of a payoff read every FlexLine the customer has held: a payment that came back on any of them within the last 6 months together with a late fee posted on any of them within the last 12 months gives 3 days, such a returned payment with no late fee within the last 12 months gives 1 day, and no payment coming back on any of them within the last 6 months gives 0. A window of the last 6 or 12 months covers entries dated fewer than that many whole months before today, a month being whole once today's day of the month has reached the entry's day of the month.

"Every FlexLine the customer has held" means every line under FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit in the customer's name, whatever its status; the entries read are the returned-payment entries and the late-fee entries on those lines.

## Input — judgement — output

| FlexLine payment returned within 6 months | FlexLine late fee within 12 months | Extra good-through days |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 3 |
| yes | no | 1 |
| no | either | 0 |


## Cases (hypothetical, payoff on 15 October)

- A FlexLine payment came back on 10 September; a FlexLine late fee posted on 10 March: 3 extra days.
- A FlexLine payment came back on 10 September; no FlexLine late fee in the last 12 months: 1 extra day.
- A FlexLine late fee on 10 September but no FlexLine payment returned since 10 March of the year before: 0 extra days.
